arxiv-1803-01516.title: A new stereo formulation not using pixel and disparity models
arxiv-1803-01516.creator: Kiyoshi Oguri Yuichiro Shibata
arxiv-1803-01516.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Kiyoshi Oguri Yuichiro Shibata. We introduce a new stereo formulation which does not use pixel and disparity models. Many problems in vision are treated as assigning each pixel a label. Disparities are labels for stereo. Such pixel-labeling problems are naturally represented in terms of energy minimization, where the energy function has two terms: one term penalizes solutions that inconsistent with the observed data, the other term enforces spatial smoothness. Graph cuts are one of the efficient methods for solving energy minimization.

arxiv-2010-11725.title: What do CNN neurons learn: Visualization & Clustering
arxiv-2010-11725.creator: Haoyue Dai
arxiv-2010-11725.description: Abstract In recent years convolutional neural networks (CNN) have shown striking progress in various tasks. However, despite the high performance, the training and prediction process remains to be a black box, leaving it a mystery to extract what neurons learn in CNN.

arxiv-2107-02423.title: Improving Text-to-Image Synthesis Using Contrastive Learning
arxiv-2107-02423.creator: Hui Ye, Xiulong Yang, Martin Takáč, Rajshekhar Sunderraman, Shihao Ji
arxiv-2107-02423.description: Abstract The goal of text-to-image synthesis is to generate a visually realistic image that matches a given text description. In practice, the captions annotated by humans for the same image have large variance in terms of contents and the choice of words.

arxiv-2109-05644.title: SHAPE: Shifted Absolute Position Embedding for Transformers
arxiv-2109-05644.creator: Shun Kiyono Sosuke Kobayashi Jun Suzuki Kentaro Inui, [2pt] RIKEN Tohoku University Preferred Networks, Inc. shun.kiyono@riken.jp , sosk@preferred.jp , {jun.suzuki, inui}@tohoku.ac.jp
arxiv-2109-05644.description: Abstract Position representation is crucial for building position-aware representations in Transformers. Existing position representations suffer from a lack of generalization to test data with unseen lengths or high computational cost. We investigate shifted absolute position embedding (SHAPE) to address both issues.

arxiv-2109-08562.title: Nonlinear simulations of tides in the convective envelopes of low-mass stars and giant gaseous planets
arxiv-2109-08562.creator: A. Astoul, A. J. Barker 1
arxiv-2109-08562.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A. Astoul, A. J. Barker 1. In close two-body astrophysical systems, such as binary stars or Hot Jupiter systems, tidal interactions often drive dynamical evolution on secular timescales. Many host stars and presumably giant gaseous planets feature a convective envelope. Tidal flows generated therein by the tidal potential of the companion can be dissipated through viscous friction, leading to the redistribution and exchange of angular momentum within the convective shell and with the companion, respectively.

arxiv-2112-07167.title: Moderate deviation expansion for fully quantum tasks
arxiv-2112-07167.creator: Navneeth Ramakrishnan, Marco Tomamichel, Mario Berta
arxiv-2112-07167.description: Abstract The moderate deviation regime is concerned with the finite block length trade-off between communication cost and error for information processing tasks in the asymptotic regime, where the communication cost approaches a capacity-like quantity and the error vanishes at the same time.

arxiv-2210-04149.title: Take a Fresh Look at Recommender Systems from an Evaluation Standpoint Conference: Proceedings of the 46th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 23–27, 2023; Taipei, Taiwan Proceedings of the 46th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research
arxiv-2210-04149.creator: Aixin Sun
arxiv-2210-04149.description: Abstract . Recommendation has become a prominent area of research in the field of Information Retrieval (IR). Evaluation is also a traditional research topic in this community. Motivated by a few counter-intuitive observations reported in recent studies, this perspectives paper takes a fresh look at recommender systems from an evaluation standpoint.

arxiv-2406-15315.title: Backward behavior and determining functionals for chevron pattern equations
arxiv-2406-15315.creator: V. K. Kalantarov 1 , H. V. Kalantarova 2 , and O. Vantzos 3
arxiv-2406-15315.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by V. K. Kalantarov 1 , H. V. Kalantarova 2 , and O. Vantzos 3. The paper is devoted to the study of the backward behavior of solutions of the initial boundary value problem for the chevron pattern equations under homogeneous Dirichlet’s boundary conditions. We prove that, as t → ∞ t\rightarrow\infty , the asymptotic behavior of solutions of the considered problem is completely determined by the dynamics of a finite set of functionals.

arxiv-2507-22973.title: Four-dimensional spectrum generating algebra for the superstring
arxiv-2507-22973.creator: Renann Lipinski Jusinskas 1, Aravindhan Srinivasan 2,3
arxiv-2507-22973.description: Abstract We derive the spectrum generating algebra for the hybrid string with manifest 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 super Poincaré symmetry in ℝ 3 , 1 × ℝ 6 \mathbb{R}^{3,1}\times\mathbb{R}^{6} . Our DDF operators establish a one-to-one correspondence with the conventional superstring spectrum, while making its four-dimensional structure manifest.

arxiv-2509-04672.title: ρ \rho -Meson Nucleon Scattering Length from CLAS Threshold Photoproduction Measurements
arxiv-2509-04672.creator: Igor I. Strakovsky, Evgeny L. Isupov, Victor Mokeev, Axel Schmidt
arxiv-2509-04672.description: Abstract Extending our study of the vector meson-nucleon scattering lengths (summary is given in Ref. Strakovsky:2021vyk ), we are focusing on the ρ \rho -meson case using recent CLAS threshold data for the reaction γ ​ p → ρ ​ p \gamma p\to\rho p within the meson–baryon reaction model CLAS:2018drk .

arxiv-2512-00236.title: Moderate Deviation Principles for Stochastic Differential Equations in Fast-Varying Markovian Environment
arxiv-2512-00236.creator: Hongjiang Qian
arxiv-2512-00236.description: Abstract In this paper, we proved moderate deviation principles for a fully coupled two-time-scale stochastic systems, where the slow process is given by stochastic differential equations with small noise, while the fast process is a rapidly changing purely jump process on finite state space.

arxiv-2601-12823.title: TreeDGS: Aerial Gaussian Splatting for Distant DBH Measurement
arxiv-2601-12823.creator: Belal Shaheen, Minh-Hieu Nguyen, Bach-Thuan Bui, Shubham, Tim Wu, Michael Fairley, Matthew David Zane, Michael Wu, James Tompkin, [2pt] Corresponding author: michael@coolant.earth
arxiv-2601-12823.description: Abstract Aerial remote sensing enables efficient large-area surveying, but accurate direct object-level measurement remains difficult in complex natural scenes. Recent advancements in 3D vision, particularly learned radiance-field representations such as NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting, have begun to raise the ceiling on reconstruction fidelity and densifiable geometry from posed imagery.

arxiv-2602-14493.title: Gaussian Mesh Renderer for Lightweight Differentiable Rendering
arxiv-2602-14493.creator: Xinpeng Liu, Fumio Okura
arxiv-2602-14493.description: Abstract 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has enabled high-fidelity virtualization with fast rendering and optimization for novel view synthesis. On the other hand, triangle mesh models still remain a popular choice for surface reconstruction but suffer from slow or heavy optimization in traditional mesh-based differentiable renderers.

pmc-10670404.title: Iron Surveillance and Management in Gastro-Intestinal Oncology Patients: A National Physician Survey †
pmc-10670404.creator: Emilie S Richard, Adriyan Hrycyshyn, Noor Salman, Alliya Remtulla Tharani, Alexandria Abbruzzino, Janet Smith, Jacob J Kachura, Michelle Sholzberg, Jeffrey D Mosko, Sami A Chadi, Ronald L Burkes, Maya Pankiw, Christine Brezden-Masley
pmc-10670404.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Purpose: Iron deficiency (ID) is a complication of gastrointestinal (GI) cancers that may manifest as iron deficiency anemia (IDA). Serum ferritin monitoring and oral iron supplementation have the limitations of being falsely elevated and poorly absorbed, respectively. This study aims to assess the discordance in surveillance, treatment practices, and awareness of ID/IDA in GI cancer patients by Canadian physicians treating these patients.

pmc-11615071.title: Metabolic signatures of combined exercise and fasting: an expanded perspective on previous telomere length findings
pmc-11615071.creator: Shamma Almuraikhy, Khaled Naja, Najeha Anwardeen, Maha Sellami, Hadaia Saleh Al-Amri, Haya Al-Sulaiti, Sara S. Bashraheel, Amina Ali Aden, Mohamed A. Elrayess
pmc-11615071.description: IntroductionAging is a complex process marked by a gradual decline in physiological function and increased susceptibility to diseases. Telomere length is frequently regarded as one of the primary biomarkers of aging. Metabolic profiles are key features in longevity and have been associated with both age and age-related diseases.

pmc-11643854.title: The Impact of Minerals on Female Fertility: A Systematic Review
pmc-11643854.creator: Celine Kapper, Patrick Stelzl, Peter Oppelt, Clara Ganhör, Ayberk Alp Gyunesh, Barbara Arbeithuber, Marlene Rezk-Füreder
pmc-11643854.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Female fertility and reproductive system disorders are influenced by a complex interplay of biological, physiological, and environmental factors. Minerals have emerged as crucial yet often overlooked elements that impact fertility and the prevalence of reproductive system disorders. Background/Objectives: This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the multifaceted role of minerals in female fertility, focusing on key areas such as oocyte quality, ovulation, embryo development, oxidative stress, miscarriage, hormonal regulation, environmental exposure, and in-vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes.

pmc-12467581.title: Effects of Moral Elevation on Children’s Implicit and Explicit Prosociality: Evidence from Behavioral and Physiological Responses
pmc-12467581.creator: Qin Wang, Xia Zhou, Lei Xun, Sylvia Terbeck
pmc-12467581.description: This study investigated how moral elevation affects children’s prosocial behavior through two experiments. In Experiment 1 (n = 99; Mage = 10.48 ± 0.86 years), children were randomly assigned to Moral Elevation, Joy, or Neutral groups. Psychophysiological measures were recorded during both the baseline and task phases, while self-reported prosocial behavior was assessed using validated scales.

pmc-12594852.title: Deciphering the molecular mechanisms of FET fusion oncoprotein–DNA hollow co-condensates
pmc-12594852.creator: Linyu Zuo, Qirui Guo, Cheng Li, Kecheng Zhang, Yancao Chen, Baiyi Jiang, Zhixing Chen, Yufei Xia, Long Qian, Lei Zhang, Zhi Qi
pmc-12594852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Biomolecules such as nucleic acids and proteins can undergo phase separation to form biomolecular condensates with diverse architectures. Here, we report that the FUS/EWS/TAF15 family fusion oncoprotein FUS-ERG forms hollow co-condensates with double-stranded DNA containing GGAA microsatellites. Through a combination of biochemical assays, super-resolution imaging, and mathematical modeling, we reveal that the interior surface of hollow co-condensates exhibits properties distinct from those of the external surface, a phenomenon we term nested asymmetric phase separation.

pmc-12617139.title: WF1. Protecting Mental Health and Managing Trauma: Building Resilience and Self-Care in Stressful Situations
pmc-12617139.creator: Organized by: WONCA Working Party on Mental Health, Marilena Anastasaki, Heather Rogers, Flavio de Silva, Fotini Anastasiou, Christos Lionis
pmc-12617139.description: BackgroundGlobal crises, humanitarian emergencies, and forced migration continue to challenge the mental health and well-being of individuals and communities. Frontline healthcare professionals, particularly those in primary care, play a pivotal role in managing psychological trauma and fostering resilience among both patients and themselves.

pmc-12772133.title: Methylation-based signature to distinguish indolent and aggressive prostate cancer
pmc-12772133.creator: Muheng Liao, Jace Webster, Amy Ly, Emily Rozycki, Christopher A Maher
pmc-12772133.description: Prostate cancer management faces significant challenges in distinguishing indolent from aggressive disease, particularly since most patients are intermediate-risk and therefore hinders the ability to recommend standardized treatment recommendations. Moreover, current prognostic tools including Gleason scoring and tumor staging demonstrate limited accuracy for predicting disease progression and tumor recurrence.

pmc-13011145.title: Surgical Management of Pancreatic Head Arteriovenous Malformation: A Case Report
pmc-13011145.creator: Anirudh Krishnan, Kellee Slater
pmc-13011145.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pancreatic arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs) are uncommon abnormalities of pancreatic blood vessels that result in direct, high-flow connections between arteries and veins. There are currently fewer than 200 reported cases in the literature of this particular anomaly. They are often clinically asymptomatic but may present with abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, or features of portal hypertension, and can resemble cystic or neoplastic lesions on imaging.

pmc-13332103.creator: María de los Ángeles Fernández-Ceballos, José M. Prieto-González, Roberto Carlos Agís-Balboa

pmc-13374439.title: First 100 migrants seeking culturally inclusive internet-based treatment for PTSD: a Mind the Gap pilot outreach study
pmc-13374439.creator: Karolina Sörman, Nitya Jayaram-Lindström, Moa Pontén, Maria Bragesjö, Karoline Kolaas, Martin Kraepelien, Samir El Alaoui, Josefin Särnholm, Olof Molander
pmc-13374439.description: IntroductionImmigrants access mental healthcare at lower rates than native-born individuals, highlighting the need for interventions and systematic assessments of scalability to reach underserved populations.AimThis study (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06193161) evaluates outreach procedures and the characteristics of the first 100 immigrants who sought internet-based treatment in Sweden for post-traumatic stress disorder.

pmc-13386900.title: Why inverse simulations overestimate optimal ankle exoskeleton assistance: the role of bi-articular coordination and joint stiffness
pmc-13386900.creator: Israel Luis, Elena M Gutierrez-Farewik, Maarten Afschrift
pmc-13386900.description: BackgroundAnkle-foot exoskeletons can reduce muscle activity and metabolic energy consumption during walking. Experimental studies consistently show that submaximal assistance, typically providing 40–60% of the biological plantarflexion moment, achieves the largest reductions in metabolic power. Inverse musculoskeletal simulations, which neglect factors such as comfort and balance, also predict that submaximal assistance is optimal, yet at higher levels than those observed experimentally.

pmc-13673507.title: Pain Severity Trajectories and Patient Profiles in Chronic Pain Patients Treated with Cannabis‐Based Medicinal Products: A k‐Means Clustering Analysis of the UK Medical Cannabis Registry
pmc-13673507.creator: Simon Erridge, Aritra Datta, Aditya Mukherjee, Dhruv Vasooja, Ross Coomber, Sushil Beri, Shaheen A Khan, Mark W Weatherall, Michael W Platt, James J Rucker, Pedro A M Mediano, Mikael H Sodergren
pmc-13673507.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cannabis‐based medicinal products (CBMPs) are increasingly prescribed for chronic pain, yet the supporting evidence remains limited and the extent to which patients differ in their response is poorly understood. This study applied longitudinal k‐means clustering to pain‐severity trajectories in patients treated with CBMPs for chronic pain to distinguish patterns of response and identify the baseline characteristics predicting them over 24 months. A cohort study was undertaken of UK Medical Cannabis Registry participants whose primary indication was chronic pain.
